summary: Late-night 5xx wave traced to connection leak in runtime proxy causing backend overload
description: Issue summary: Between 23:40 and 01:20 UTC on 2026-03-10 we observed an elevated 5xx rate from CloudCanary customers routed to prod-us-east. Errors surfaced as 502/504 and occasional 500s from the API Gateway with upstream/runtime timeouts or connection resets. Impact: CloudCanary reporting degraded realtime summarization performance and increased latency; automated retries caused client-side backoffs and user-visible errors. Scope: Affected a subset of dedicated customer capacity pools using redwood-7b-v1; roughly 8% of requests in us-east and spillover into us-west via cross-region fallback. Immediate customer impact documented by CloudCanary support logs and error samples attached below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use CloudCanary dedicated credentials against prod-us-east endpoint (same routing policy used by customer). 2) Issue a sustained mix of streaming and non-streaming requests at moderate concurrency (~50 concurrent sessions) with 16k context windows. 3) Observe API Gateway 502/504 rates rising after ~20 minutes, upstream connection resets on runtime-proxy, and runtimes report half-open sockets in metrics.
logs: 2026-03-10T23:48:12Z apigw svc=proxy status=502 upstream=runtime-proxy-17 msg=upstream reset by peer
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler warmup caused short-term capacity gap — ruled out after autoscaler metrics show no scale-down events in the window.
Memory/CPU on runtimes within normal bounds; however runtime-proxy metrics show steadily increasing 'leaked_connection_count' and 'fd_pending_close' beginning ~23:30 UTC.

Packet captures from runtime-proxy indicate TCP FIN not being delivered to upstream until keepalive expiry; suggestive of improper connection lifecycle handling in proxy between api-gateway and serving-runtime.
Correlation found between a recent runtime-proxy config roll (PR 438) that changed connection timeout handling and a subsequent small flag toggle rolled out to 20% of proxy pods at 23:00 UTC.
Repro on staging with same flag toggled reproduced connection leak after sustained streaming requests; engineer reproduction run attached to PR discussion.
Customer-side retry loops amplified load on healthy backends once proxy started queuing half-open sockets, creating cascading 502/504s at the API layer.
comments: Sana Iqbal (2026-03-10): Customer reported sudden 5xx increase around 23:45 UTC. Collected sample request IDs and start/stop times. Escalating to SRE on-call.
Oliver Grant (SRE) (2026-03-11): Confirmed elevated 'leaked_connection_count' on a subset of runtime-proxy pods. Isolating pods with the new flag and draining them to stop flow-through.
Marta Ruiz (Service Owner) (2026-03-11): Initiated rollback of proxy flag to 0% for all prod-us-east proxy pods at 00:30 UTC. Monitoring for improvement.
CloudCanary Support (2026-03-11): Noted immediate drop in client errors after rollback; however some 502s persisted for ~15 minutes due to backlog and request retries.
Oliver Grant (2026-03-12): Running follow-up load test in staging. Patch candidate identified in PR 441 to properly close idle connections; scheduling hotfix rollout.
resolution: Workaround: Rolled back the connection timeout flag on runtime-proxy to previous stable configuration across prod-us-east at 00:30 UTC which stopped the leak from growing. Post-rollback, API Gateway 5xx rate decreased to baseline within ~18 minutes. Permanent fix: Backported patch from staging (PR 441) to ensure proactive socket closure and improved keepalive handling; hotfix rollout scheduled for 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC with canary and 30-minute observation windows. Follow-ups: add dashboard alert for 'leaked_connection_count' and fd_pending_close; add a test in the runtime-proxy CI that simulates long-lived streaming connections to catch regressions. Customer communication: Notified CloudCanary CS about root cause, mitigation steps, and planned hotfix; offered a post-incident retrospective and configuration review for dedicated pools.
postmortem_actions: Action: Ship PR 441 to prod with staged rollout and automatic rollback if leaked_connection_count increases > 5% above baseline.
Action: Add an SLO alarm for leaked_connection_count and fd_pending_close to trigger a PagerDuty for P1 on-call.
Action: Update runbook to include flag rollout checklist and immediate rollback criteria.
Action: Notify Dedicated customers about safe flag rollout windows and create a preflight test for future proxy changes.
resolution_status: Hotfix scheduled; partial mitigation completed (flag rollback). Monitoring and alerting actions in progress.
